This was a relatively short game but I enjoyed it. The music and sound effects are definitely a stand out. The story is is okay but picks up a bit closer to the end. These game reminds of things like Limbo with trial and error. The bosses are mostly, run left and right to avoid being hit or just run away, doesn't make them particularly interesting or memorable. Overall, it's a fun play but the memory of it probably won't stick with you for long.

The Deed was good fun. You’re setting up a murder and trying to pin it on someone else, so your choices matter when it comes to getting away with it. A neat little twist on a murder mystery, and I enjoyed it.

a short and sweet hollow-knight-like experience. area design was great, not a massive fan of the overall art style though. platforming is solid, combat is a bit lackluster and is often just swing your sword as much as you can while dogding very telegraphed attacks. the harder bosses don't really have a more difficult moveset they just telegraph their attacks slightly less which isn't a great way to add difficulty. overall this was very easy to pick up and very easy to put down

Basically a clicker game with an optional spreadsheet (find out what combinations of game genres work with each other).

No depth at all... but still surprisingly fun! 

My standards are very low for clicker games.

My only crisisism is that it isn't larger. Everything about this game is just... really small. From map sizes to weapon variety, to amound of non-essential "dungeons".

That being said. this is probably the gold standard for a non-bethesda scrolls-like. I am gonna be keeping a close eye on these developers, I am really looking forward to whatever they do next.

An amazing experience. The atmosphere is top notch, and that iconic thick fog combined with the updated, creepy sound design instantly sucks you into the town. Moving the camera behind James's shoulder completely changes the vibe, making every encounter with monsters feel way more claustrophobic, intense, and genuinely scary, while the resource management keeps the tension high. The only downside is that the game feels a bit too long, and some areas like the hospital get dragged out, making the combat feel a little repetitive toward the end. Still, it completely honors the tragic emotional core of the original story while looking beautiful, so it is a must-play for any horror fan.

Its confusing to me why this was packaged as a DLC. I didn't think the main story of the base game really was set up for DLC after the ending. So a year later after I have forgotten most everything about this game and its story to come back for two hours and basically just have 3 missions that should have just been in the base game is odd. Its still good, just feels like cut content.

This is fun.  It's super fun, and it's a building/combat game that I can play with my 8 year old kid and not feel even a little bit bad about.  There's a decent plot, even!  Ok, sure, it's ankle-deep, but it's just a blast.  And any time you want to take yourself too seriously (because, like, your kid just destroyed your super cool armor by 'accidentally' smacking you during combat again), the game is there to remind you that you're wearing bits of dead ants strapped on with grass and you just can't, lol, you're just not that cool.

Ninja Gaiden: Ragebound is a fantastic game, I've been a fan of the series for years. The gameplay is thrilling, offering a perfect blend of challenge and excitement that keeps you coming back for more. The soundtrack is absolutely captivating, enhancing the overall experience and drawing you deeper into the action. The level design is another standout feature, with beautifully crafted environments that are both visually stunning and strategically engaging. This game truly feels like a worthy continuation of the Ninja Gaiden legacy, and I can’t recommend it enough! 10/10

One of the best games I've ever played. You feel like you're really on an adventure and building relationships with the characters, and not only the companions. The world is so interactive, it makes it easy to immerse yourself in it. The story and the plot twists are mind-blowing, and I love how everything you do and every interaction you have has a meaning to it. The only negative I can think of is that it would be nice to have an epilogue showing what you do after the main story, but if my only complaint is that I want more, I guess there really are no negatives.
